title: Countertop Dish Racks: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Countertop Dish Racks: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

A countertop dish rack holds washed plates, bowls, cups and cutlery while they drain. It only works if it fits the free worktop beside the sink, clears the wall cupboards with plates in it, takes your plate and bowl sizes, and sends the water into the sink rather than onto the worktop. Use these checks before choosing one. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

1. Worktop space: Length and depth beside the sink.
2. Cupboard height: Tallest plate plus the rack.
3. Plates and bowls: Your largest plate and bowl.
4. Drainage: Water into the sink, not the worktop.

title: Clothes Airers: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Clothes Airers: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

A clothes airer is a folding rack for drying laundry indoors or outside. It only works well if it fits the floor when it is open, it has enough rail for your wash, long items can hang without touching the floor or the rail below, and it folds small enough to store. Use these checks before choosing one. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

1. Floor space open: Wings out, and room to walk past.
2. Drying length: Metres of rail for one wash.
3. Drop below each rail: Long items need height.
4. Folded size and load: Where it goes, and the weight.

title: Clothes Rails: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Clothes Rails: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

A clothes rail, also called a clothes rack or garment rail, is a freestanding frame with a hanging rail, often on castors and sometimes with a shelf for shoes or boxes. It is handy in a small bedroom, a hallway or a room without a wardrobe, but only if it fits the floor space and the height, and holds the weight of your clothes. Use these checks before choosing one. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

1. Footprint: Measure the floor, and the rail ends.
2. Height: Your longest item on its hanger.
3. Load: Compare the load with your clothes.
4. Castors and floor: Check brakes, carpet and thresholds.

title: Cupboard Shelf Risers: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Cupboard Shelf Risers: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

A shelf riser, sometimes sold as a shelf insert, turns one tall cupboard shelf into two levels for plates, mugs, bowls or tins. 3. Room on top: Leave space above to lift things out.

title: Curtain Poles: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Curtain Poles: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

A curtain pole, also called a curtain rod, is screwed to the wall or ceiling on brackets and holds curtains on rings, eyelets or tabs. 3. Bracket space: Room above the window and in front.

title: A Narrow Gap? Measure These 4 Things Before Buying a Storage Cart
caption:
A Narrow Gap? Measure These 4 Things Before Buying a Storage Cart

A cart can look narrow enough in a photograph and still be awkward to use. The available space may change near the floor, a handle may project beyond the shelf, or there may be nowhere to pull the cart out. Use these four checks to decide whether a movable cart, a fixed shelf or no additional unit makes sense for your space.

1. Narrowest gap: Measure at several heights, not only at the top.
2. Usable depth: Check doors, handles and the space behind the cart.
3. Floor obstacles: Skirting boards, pipes and uneven floors use up space.
4. Pull-out route: Leave a usable route for getting items in and out.

caption:
Over-the-Door Hooks: Check These 4 Things Before You Buy

Over-the-door storage avoids drilling, but it depends on details that are easy to miss: the thickness of the door, the gap between the door and its frame, and what happens when the door opens and closes. Use these checks to decide whether an over-the-door hanger suits your door or whether a wall hook or freestanding rack makes more sense. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

2. Top gap: Check the gap above the door when it is closed.
3. Projection: Allow for the rack and your things sticking out.
4. Load and movement: Check the load limit and how it moves with the door.

Over-the-Sink Dish Racks: Measure These 4 Things First

An over-the-sink rack frees counter space only if it suits the sink, the tap and the wall around them. Frame racks stand on the counter on either side of the sink; roll-up racks and sink baskets rest on the rim. Either way, a few measurements decide whether the rack sits level, lets the tap move and drains where it should. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

2. Tap clearance: Leave room to turn, lift and swing the tap.
3. Overhead space: Measure up to wall cabinets, shelves or a window.
4. Drainage and load: Water should drip into the bowl. Check the load.

caption:
Over-the-Toilet Storage: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

3. Pipes and floor: Look behind the toilet for pipes and valves.

caption:

Slim shoe cabinets can be less than 25 cm deep, which makes them useful in narrow hallways, but the shallow depth is also their limit. Large trainers and boots may not fit, the flaps need room to open, and a tall, shallow cabinet has to be fixed to the wall. Use these checks before choosing a cabinet. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

1. Shoe size: Compare your largest shoes with the maximum size.
2. Depth and flaps: Leave room for open flaps and for people to pass.
3. Wall and skirting: Tall, shallow units need fixing to the wall.
4. Real capacity: Listed pair counts depend on shoe size.

title: Under-Bed Storage: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy
caption:
Under-Bed Storage: Measure These 4 Things Before You Buy

The space under a bed looks generous until you measure it. Side rails, slats, centre legs and the floor itself all limit what fits, and a box that fits underneath may still be awkward to pull out. Use these checks to compare boxes, bags and drawers, or to decide that another spot would work better. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

1. Lowest clearance: Measure to the lowest rail or bar, not to the mattress.
2. Usable depth: Centre legs and bars can stop a box halfway.
3. Pull-out room: Leave floor space beside the bed to open it.

caption:
Under-Shelf Baskets: Check Shelf Thickness and 3 More Things

Under-shelf baskets add a layer of storage without drilling, but they hang from the shelf itself. If the arms are too tight they will not slide on; too loose and the basket tilts. Use these checks to see whether a basket suits your cupboard, bookcase or desk before you buy. This guide is a planning aid, not a compatibility guarantee.

3. Space below: Measure the gap to the next shelf or the worktop.
4. Load and open sides: Keep it light. Things can slide out of open sides.
